comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause, proof, and defect origin

### Mechanism (proven at runtime, twice, independently)

`_hash_basis(..., at_current_gate_ref=True)` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:246-260`)
catches `Exception` around the gate-ref resolution, logs a WARNING, and returns the in-place
working tree as the hashing basis. Its only production caller is the claim-gate freshness
re-check (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:605-613`, inside `compute_validity` for
`kind == plan-review`).

### Discriminating experiment (E1)

One signed attested attestation pinning `dep.py`; the dependency drifts and LANDS on
`origin/main`; the working tree is rolled back to the reviewed bytes. Varying ONLY whether the
gate ref resolves:

```
gate ref resolvable   -> {'ok': False, 'verdict': 'stale-code'}   claim BLOCKED
gate ref UNRESOLVABLE -> {'ok': True,  'verdict': 'certified'}    claim ALLOWED
```

Run independently twice (orchestrator + a blind investigator) with the same result. This kills
the docstring's own justification — "the conservative direction, since the checkout normally
contains the drift" — because the degradation is demonstrably the PERMISSIVE direction whenever
the checkout does not contain the drift.

### Violated authority (legitimacy = defect)

* `docs/plan-review-gate.md:1567` — `| Claim gate | **fail-closed** | a missing/stale
  plan-review attestation BLOCKS the claim |`; `:1574` "reserve fail-closed for the claim gate".
* `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` — "attested **fails closed** — it never serves the wrong tree";
  itemizing "the gate does **not** fall back to some other tree".
* `docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md:46` — "keeping the fallback fail-closed".
* `docs/plan-review-gate.md:939` (operator ruling 39f8-ae7c) — "it never silently resolves the
  gate to its default".

The premise the authorization rests on is false in both environments where the fallback fires:
the review-bot's clone holds a PATCHSET, and the deployed MCP box's `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`
working tree is pinned at container-boot clone time (`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh`,
`git clone --filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch main`) with NO subsequent
`git fetch`/`pull` of the tree, while `refs/remotes/origin/main` does advance. That checkout is
systematically BEHIND main — it lacks the drift rather than containing it.

### Blast radius

* **Review-bot (the messenger).** `clone_change_ref` does `git init` + `git fetch <url>
  <patchset-ref>` with no `origin` remote, so the fallback fires on 100% of runs. Its consumer
  is `bugfix_size_gate.classify_plan_review_attestation`, whose
  `ACCEPTED_VERDICTS = {certified, stale-code, stale-head}` absorbs both outcomes. **The
  observed log line has no verdict consequence.** The review-bot surfaced the defect; it is
  not the victim.
* **Claim gate (the victim).** `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true`. On the box the ref
  itself resolves, but the same broad `except` also swallows `_cache.acquire` failures —
  `repo_snapshot._ensure_blobs_present` is explicitly "BEST-EFFORT and silent on failure" on a
  blobless clone, so a failed blob top-up degrades to that stale boot-time tree.
  *Labelled: verified by code reading, not reproduced on the box.*
* **Signing side unaffected.** `dependency_hashes` / `_rehash` take the no-flag branch
  (`current_code_root()`), so **no signed attestation's `verified_at_sha` or manifest hashes
  were ever computed on a substituted basis.** `verified_at_sha` pins the SIGNING basis only;
  nothing records the VERIFY basis — which is why the substitution is undetectable.

### Visibility (why "silent" is the anomaly)

`compute_validity` -> `{valid, reason, verdict}` (+ `health`, `registry_drift`);
`claim_gate_check` -> `{ok, reason, verdict}`. **No basis field, no sidecar, no telemetry.**
The single trace is one `logger.warning`. This is out of step with the codebase's own
conventions: `bugfix_size_gate`'s `infra`/abstain bucket, `registry_drift` surfaced on
`compute_validity`'s own result (ADR 0053), `_UNPINNED` ("honest and fail-closed"),
`stale-store`, the close gate's `unavailable` + structured event, and the DET floor's recorded
abstention. Tightest comparison: **inside `claim_gate_check` itself**, an unavailable *signing
subsystem* fails closed with `verdict: "error"`, while an unavailable *basis* degrades silently.

### Defect origin — `caused_by` 72d9-8fbd-3a9e-48a6 (athletic-esthetical-polecat)

Introducing commit **`2e2fe3f7d25c`** (2026-07-24, trailer
`rebar-ticket: 72d9-8fbd-3a9e-48a6`). Established with `git log -L218,262:…manifest.py -w -C -M`;
`a9aed66ce412` in the same range is a Ruff-hygiene no-op and was walked through as a carrier.

**Divergence from what a whole-file blame would say, recorded per protocol.** The broad-except
degrade itself is OLDER — `b25fafcd188b` (2026-06-27, epic `raze-vet-ditch` story
`e308-daf0-d765-40d3` / `piney-gold-day`) — so a naive blame attributes there. That is wrong:
under `b25fafcd188b` the drift check was the tautology 72d9 exists to fix, so the degrade could
not flip any verdict. `2e2fe3f7d25c` made the check consequential AND repointed it from a pinned
SHA to `origin/main`, creating the obligation "every claim environment must resolve
`origin/main`" while carrying the now-consequential degrade forward unreconciled against the
documented fail-closed posture. Unmet obligation, hence `close_class=regression`.

The review-bot's consumption (`1920dc9fe559`, 2026-08-03) only made the condition visible in
logs; it post-dates 72d9 and did not create it.

### Two gaps the repair must respect

1. The existing pin `test_ref_coherence.py::test_hash_basis_resolution` asserts only the fallback
   *path* and *does not crash* — never a resulting VERDICT. The suite was structurally blind to
   this flip, so the RED oracle must be verdict-level.
2. `source=local` stays exempt: there the working tree is the correct, documented back-out, not a
   substitution. Only the attested-but-unresolvable arm is defective.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Observed in the DEPLOYED review-bot's logs (2026-08-28), once per run:

```
current gate-ref snapshot unavailable; hashing the working tree
  File "/app/src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py", line 254, in _hash_basis
    sha = resolve_ref(gate_source.default_ref(root), root, fetch=False)
  File "/app/src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py", line 292, in resolve_ref
rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.SnapshotRefError: cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '/tmp/reviewbot-cjb9jh6c'.
```

## Proven mechanism

`_hash_basis(repo_root, *, at_current_gate_ref=True)`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:246-260`) wraps the gate-ref resolution in a
bare `except Exception`, logs a WARNING, and returns `_config.repo_root(repo_root)` —
the in-place working tree — as the hashing basis.

Its sole production caller is the CLAIM-GATE freshness re-check
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:605-613`, inside `compute_validity` for
`kind == plan-review`), which re-hashes the attestation's SIGNED dependency paths
against that basis to decide `stale-code`.

Signing-time hashing (`manifest.py:398 dependency_hashes`, `attest.py:237 _rehash`)
uses the OTHER branch (`current_code_root()`), so **no signed attestation's
`verified_at_sha` or manifest hashes are affected**. The defect is entirely on the
VERIFY side.

### The fallback is fail-OPEN, contrary to its own stated rationale

The docstring claims the degradation is "the conservative direction, since the
checkout normally contains the drift". A runtime experiment falsifies this. With one
signed attestation and a genuinely drifted `origin/main`, toggling ONLY whether the
gate ref resolves:

* gate ref resolvable  -> `{'ok': False, 'verdict': 'stale-code'}`  (claim BLOCKED)
* gate ref unresolvable -> `{'ok': True,  'verdict': 'certified'}`  (claim ALLOWED)

Whenever the working tree happens to match the reviewed content while the gate ref has
moved (a worktree not yet fast-forwarded; a checkout pinned at the reviewed SHA), the
substituted basis reports NO drift and the gate certifies a stale attestation.

### Violated authority

`docs/plan-review-gate.md:1566-1574`:

    | Claim gate | **fail-closed** | a missing/stale plan-review attestation BLOCKS the claim |
    ... reserve fail-closed for the claim gate.

and ADR 0002 (`docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md:46`) "keeping the fallback
fail-closed". `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true` in this project's
`rebar.toml`, so the gate is live.

### Reachability

The `except Exception` catches far more than a missing ref: any failure of
`resolve_ref` OR `_cache.acquire` (snapshot materialization) — disk pressure, a
corrupt/evicted cache entry, a lock timeout, a transient git fault — degrades the
same way, on the on-box MCP server (`REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`) where
claims are actually decided. The only trace is a WARNING line.

In the review-bot's own clone (`gerrit_client.py:396 clone_change_ref` does
`git init` + `git fetch <url> <patchset-ref>` with NO `origin` remote) the ref can
NEVER resolve, so the fallback fires on 100% of runs. There the consumer is the
bugfix-size gate, whose `ACCEPTED_VERDICTS = {certified, stale-code, stale-head}`
absorbs both outcomes — so the observed log line does not change the review-bot's
vote. The review-bot is the messenger, not the victim.

## What is NOT the defect

The fallback's EXISTENCE is intended and documented (ADR 0002 "Shared ref-resolution
boundary"; the operator-approved decision on ticket 72d9-8fbd-3a9e-48a6 —
"source=local config or an unresolvable ref degrades to the working tree"; and the
existing test `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ref_coherence.py::test_hash_basis_resolution`
asserts "an unresolvable ref -> degrade to the working tree (never crash)").
The fix must NOT remove it. The defect is that the substitution is invisible to the
consumer, so the fail-closed claim gate silently becomes fail-open.

## Expected Behavior

When the claim gate's drift check cannot obtain the configured ATTESTED basis, it must
not certify. The substitution must be visible to the verdict consumer, and the claim
must be blocked with a reason naming the unobtainable basis. A configured
`source=local` gate is UNCHANGED: there the working tree is the correct, documented
basis, not a degradation.

## Approach

1. Keep `_hash_basis`'s public behaviour and signature exactly as today (the tested,
   ADR-documented contract). Extract the gate-ref resolution into a sibling that also
   reports whether it degraded, and have `_hash_basis` delegate to it — preserving the
   ADR 0002 "ONE shared ref-resolution boundary" invariant.
2. In `compute_validity`'s plan-review drift arm, consume the degradation signal: when
   the gate is configured ATTESTED and the basis degraded, return the existing
   `stale-code` verdict with a reason naming the unobtainable gate ref, instead of
   comparing hashes against a substituted tree.
3. Reuse the EXISTING `stale-code` literal deliberately: it is already in
   `bugfix_size_gate.ACCEPTED_VERDICTS`, so the review-bot's vote is unchanged (it
   already lands on `stale-code` for most runs today), while the claim gate blocks.
   No new verdict literal, no change to `KNOWN_VERDICTS`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ref_coherence.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With an attested gate config, a signed attestation whose dependency drifted on the
      gate ref, and a working tree still matching the signed content: the claim gate
      returns `ok=False` / `verdict=stale-code` when the gate ref CANNOT be resolved
      (today it returns `ok=True` / `certified`).
- [ ] The denial reason names the unobtainable gate ref rather than claiming the files
      drifted.
- [ ] With the gate ref RESOLVABLE, every existing behaviour is unchanged: committed
      drift in a signed dependency still invalidates; an unrelated committed change and an
      uncommitted working-tree edit still do NOT.
- [ ] A configured `source=local` gate is unchanged (working-tree basis on both sides; no
      degradation reported).
- [ ] `_hash_basis(..., at_current_gate_ref=True)` still returns the working-tree path on
      an unresolvable ref (never raises) — `test_hash_basis_resolution` stays green.
- [ ] No new verdict literal: `bugfix_size_gate.KNOWN_VERDICTS` is untouched and the
      review-bot's bucket for these runs is unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default pytest suite exit zero.

the claim-gate drift arm consumes the degradation signal and fails closed with stale-code
